message: Step ":hammer: Tests" does not define timeout_in_minutes.
why: Buildkite has no default timeout. Without timeout_in_minutes, a hung or degraded step can run indefinitely and consume agent capacity.
suggestion: Add timeout_in_minutes to prevent unbounded execution; when the work runs inside a plugin, set the value above that plugin's own internal limit so a normal run is not cut short.
measurementHint: Monitor the step's typical duration and allow for normal variance. Plugin steps need headroom above the plugin's own internal limit.
aiHandoff: Review .buildkite/pipeline.yml step ":hammer: Tests" and add a timeout_in_minutes value above any plugin-internal limit.

message: Step ":hammer: Tests" runs heavy work on every build and has no if_changed.
why: Commits that only touch files the step ignores (for example documentation) still pay its full cost. if_changed omits a step when the build's changed files match none of its globs.
suggestion: Add if_changed with glob patterns covering the files this step consumes (requires a pipeline uploaded with buildkite-agent pipeline upload and an agent that applies it by default, 3.103.0+). Keep deploy steps off if_changed: on the default branch the changed-file set only reflects the previous commit, so a multi-commit push can skip a needed deployment.
measurementHint: Count the share of recent commits whose changed files fall outside the globs. That share is the fraction of builds this step can skip.
aiHandoff: Review .buildkite/pipeline.yml step ":hammer: Tests": add if_changed globs for its input files.

message: Pipeline runs steps concurrently but no step sets cancel_on_build_failing.
why: Without the fast-fail attribute, a failing job leaves its concurrent siblings running to natural completion, occupying agents for results that cannot change the verdict.
suggestion: Add cancel_on_build_failing: true to the steps whose results cannot change the verdict once the build is failing. Teams that fix all failures in one pass may deliberately keep lanes running; retries of canceled siblings are also subject to the same policy until the source failure is retried, so retry source failures first.
measurementHint: Compare total agent time of failing builds before and after adding the attribute. Cancellation saves only the window between the first hard failure and natural completion of the siblings.
aiHandoff: Review .buildkite/pipeline.yml: add cancel_on_build_failing to steps that cannot change the verdict, starting near step ":hammer: Tests".

message: Step ":hammer: Tests" installs dependencies without a cache.
why: Every build starts from a clean checkout, so dependency directories are re-downloaded and re-installed on every run.
suggestion: Add dependency caching: a pipeline `cache:` attribute on hosted agents, the official cache plugin, or `buildkite-agent cache save/restore` keyed on the lockfile.
measurementHint: Compare the install command's duration across builds before and after adding the cache, and expect a cache miss after lockfile changes.
aiHandoff: Review .buildkite/pipeline.yml step ":hammer: Tests": add dependency caching or colocate the install with the step that consumes it.

message: Step ":package: Build" runs package script "build" through npm run.
why: For simple package-script execution on recent Node.js, node --run can avoid npm startup overhead. It is not a drop-in replacement when npm-specific behavior is required.
suggestion: Replace npm run with node --run for simple package-script execution when no npm-specific behavior is needed.
measurementHint: Compare the step duration before and after the change, and verify that the script still receives the same arguments and environment it needs.
aiHandoff: Review .buildkite/pipeline.yml step ":package: Build" running `npm run build`. Only replace it with `node --run build` after checking the collected compatibility evidence: Repository scan found no visible .npmrc file, matching pre/post lifecycle script, or npm-specific environment reference.
